brief: Make a vacant mall unit useful through a small community pilot.

sources.title: A food hall
sources.summary: Independent kitchens share tables and repeat visitors.
sources.body: Independent kitchens serve affordable meals around shared tables. Visitors can linger and meet neighbors. Food preparation needs a clean area separate from dusty work. The pilot must fit in one vacant mall unit.
sources.contribution: Shared meals and informal social time.

sources.title: A tool library
sources.summary: Borrow tools and learn practical repair from peers.
sources.body: A lending collection reduces the cost of occasional repairs. Volunteer repair sessions let neighbors teach one another. Some repairs generate dust and noise; trained supervision and separate work surfaces are needed.
sources.contribution: Borrowing tools and peer repair learning.

contributions: Make waiting for a repair useful through shared meals.
Borrow tools and get peer help completing a repair.
interaction: Use the same visit while keeping food preparation separate from dusty repairs.
replacement: Make waiting useful through short peer-taught lessons instead of a meal.
reviewFocus: Does the result actually connect waiting and social activity, and preserve the practical separation constraint?

brief: Help a small team prepare a field visit without dependable connectivity.

sources.title: A pocket field plan
sources.summary: A local plan stays available without a network.
sources.body: A phone stores the complete visit plan and records observations offline. No essential action requires connectivity. People can revise the plan locally and reconcile changes after returning.
sources.contribution: Offline availability and explicit later reconciliation.

sources.title: A shared coordination board
sources.summary: A visible board lets people claim responsibilities.
sources.body: Team members claim tasks and announce handoffs. The online version uses instant presence updates to avoid duplicate work. Responsibility and the last acknowledged handoff are visible to everyone.

contributions: All essential work remains possible offline.
Make responsibility and acknowledged handoffs visible.
interaction: Retain useful coordination while exposing uncertainty when updates cannot be shared.
replacement: Use a printed plan with handwritten changes, reconciled after the visit.
reviewFocus: Does the synthesis quietly assume live connectivity, and does it distinguish an acknowledged handoff from a stale copy?

brief: Create a small neighborhood exhibition that can change through participation.

sources.title: An oral history cabinet
sources.summary: Residents contribute memories with control over attribution.
sources.body: Residents record short memories and choose whether to be named. They can withdraw a recording. Multiple accounts of the same event may conflict, and the archive keeps those disagreements visible.
sources.contribution: Personal testimony with attribution and withdrawal choices.

sources.title: A changing model street
sources.summary: Visitors rearrange a model to propose neighborhood futures.
sources.body: Visitors move buildings and public spaces in a small physical model. Each arrangement proposes a possible future. A photograph records the arrangement and its author's explanation before the next visitor changes it.
sources.contribution: Reversible proposals expressed through spatial arrangement.

contributions: Keep conflicting memories and contributor control visible.
Let visitors make reversible proposals in a spatial model.
interaction: Connect accounts of the past to proposed futures without making one account authoritative.
replacement: Let contributors withdraw their material while retaining a visible gap explaining that an account was removed.
reviewFocus: Do disagreement and withdrawal survive the synthesis, or does the story become falsely unified?
